statement: A provider-agnostic finding schema must precede any cross-cloud prioritisation, and it must retain identity and exposure semantics that generic vulnerability formats discard.
evidence: Three providers reduced to one schema without losing IAM or reachability signal.

principle: Do not inherit another tool's severity
statement: Prioritisation should rest on observable configuration facts rather than vendor severity labels, which are frequently absent and always context-free.
evidence: Severity null on 100% of 445 open-source scanner findings.

principle: Rank the unit the analyst acts on
statement: Aggregate rule-level findings to the resource an operator would remediate; ranking rule violations individually inflates the queue and flattens the score distribution.
evidence: 340 resources from 1,009 findings; tie concentration fell from 35.3% to 20.9%.

statement: Train and evaluate on the ordering of a working set, because that is the task an analyst performs and the task the evaluation metric measures.
evidence: Set-to-ranking targets support direct Kendall tau evaluation.

principle: Adapt the prioritisation framework to the artefact
statement: Frameworks built for software vulnerabilities need recalibration for misconfigurations, where the flaw itself is the exploit and no exploit code exists.
evidence: Recalibration moved 366 findings out of a single collapsed class.

statement: When training instances are sampled with replacement from a resource pool, both splits and confidence intervals must operate on resources, or results are optimistic.
evidence: Zero cross-split overlap enforced; intervals clustered on 45 test resources.

principle: Select on the capability you need, not the one that is easy to measure
statement: Output format is learnable through fine-tuning; ranking ability is not. Select base models on task performance and treat formatting as a training objective.
evidence: Qwen JSON validity 73.3% -> 100% after training, while its ranking advantage persisted.

principle: Small models suffice for narrow prioritisation
statement: A 3-billion-parameter model fine-tuned on roughly 1,200 examples reaches expert-level agreement, allowing fully local deployment without sending findings to an external service.
evidence: tau 0.848 against expert consensus on a 16 GB consumer GPU.

statement: Report agreement of the system with itself under input reordering alongside agreement with the reference standard; the former bounds how far the latter can be trusted.
evidence: Stability 0.680 against tau 0.745 — self-agreement is the lower figure.

statement: Treat generated justifications as claims to be verified against the input, and report the unsupported proportion as a first-class metric.
evidence: Grounding precision 0.595; 40% of claims unsupported despite 100% explanation coverage.

principle: Never evaluate against your own generator
statement: A rule system used to produce training targets must be reported as a baseline. Confirmatory evaluation requires a reference standard independent of the training signal.
evidence: Model 0.848 vs composite 0.800 against experts; p = 0.51, not significant.

statement: Where stability is below agreement and a material share of explanations are unsupported, the appropriate deployment is analyst-assisted triage, not autonomous remediation ordering.
evidence: Stability 0.680, grounding 0.595, and no significant advantage over a rule system.
